prompt:
It's the start of the week and before I get buried I want to get properly on top of a few property things that have been nagging me. Three of them in particular.

First, the roof on the top-floor unit at our Ridgeview property, the one I flagged back in May for missing shingles with water coming through the ceiling, where I opened a maintenance ticket because it was clearly past a simple patch job. The owner and the vendor went back and forth on it after that and I got copied on some of it, but I've completely lost the thread. Piece together for me where it actually landed: what got approved, the scope and the dollar figure that got signed off, and who the vendor is. And I really need to know whether the work has already happened, because my gut says the repair may have gone ahead weeks ago and yet our maintenance ticket is still sitting there open, and I don't think anyone has the close-out tracked anywhere on our operations board. If there's nothing on the board holding the close-out, put something there so it has a home, since there's a follow-up vendor walk-through coming and I need the resident in that top-floor unit to get proper notice before anyone shows up. While you're at it, confirm the vendor is actually locked in for that walk-through, because if he hasn't confirmed his attendance I need to know today. Drop a note to the maintenance team about coordinating resident access for that walk-through, and send Brooke a short update letting her know the property side has the close-out in hand and asking her to make sure the vendor confirms the walk-through so I can give the resident notice.

Second, that preventive-maintenance push across my west-cluster properties that I've been running point on as the onsite lead. It was supposed to be wrapped by the end of June and I really don't think it got there. Find out where it actually stands, post an update to the team and pull in our maintenance lead to nail down whatever's still outstanding, and get the tracking on it brought current instead of just sitting stale.

Third, there was a garbage disposal problem at one of my Las Palmas units that one of the techs kicked over to our maintenance lead for a parts approval a couple of weeks back. I want to know whether that's still stuck. If it's still sitting there waiting on the approval, push it forward so the replacement can actually get scheduled and done, and make sure it isn't just quietly dying on the board.

Once you've worked through all three, give me the full rundown.

criteria.criterion: The Agent creates a Linear issue to track the close-out of the Ridgeview top-floor unit roof section repair.
criteria.evidence: See OE 7, OE 8, OE 10. Look for a Linear issue-creation action (save_issue) on the Property Ops project (proj_001, team_001) whose title/subject concerns the Ridgeview top-floor unit roof section repair or its close-out. Confirm the issue was actually created.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'if there's nothing on the board holding the close-out, put something there so it has a home.' Zero Linear issues reference Ridgeview/roof/MT-2026-047, so the agent must create one to track the close-out of the approved repair.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Ridgeview roof close-out issue references the approved vendor Pete Donovan and the approved $8,400 roof section repair scope (or similar).
criteria.evidence: See OE 3, OE 4, OE 5, OE 10. Check the created Linear issue's description for the approved vendor Pete Donovan and the approved amount $8,400 (roof section repair). Reference to the originating ticket MT-2026-047 and/or the 2026-07-13 walk-through is a plus.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the agent to establish 'what got approved, the scope and the dollar figure that got signed off, and who the vendor is' and then put the close-out on the board. The tracking issue must carry that substance: vendor Pete Donovan and the $8,400 roof section repair, both grounded in the owner-approval email (thread 0133155c8a154ab1) and the Make-Ready record rec8b679d92f30753.

criteria.criterion: The Agent posts a message in the #maintenance channel (id C001) about the Ridgeview roof repair follow-up.
criteria.evidence: See OE 6, OE 11. Look for a Slack message sent (slack_send_message) to the #maintenance channel (name '#maintenance' or id 'C001') concerning the Ridgeview roof repair follow-up. Confirm the post was actually sent.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'drop a note to the maintenance team about coordinating resident access for that walk-through.' The maintenance team's home channel is #maintenance (C001), where roof-repair coordination belongs.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's #maintenance message asks the team to coordinate resident access/notice for the Ridgeview top-floor unit ahead of the 2026-07-13 walk-through.
criteria.evidence: See OE 5, OE 11. Check the content of the #maintenance message: it should ask the maintenance team to coordinate resident access / advance notice for the top-floor unit ahead of the 2026-07-13 vendor walk-through.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt's stated purpose for the note is that the resident 'get proper notice before anyone shows up' for the follow-up vendor walk-through. criteria.criterion: The Agent creates an email draft to Brooke Phillips ([brooke.phillips@starpm.com](mailto:brooke.phillips@starpm.com)) about the Ridgeview roof repair close-out.
criteria.evidence: See OE 9, OE 12. Look for an email draft (create_draft) addressed to brooke.phillips@starpm.com regarding the Ridgeview roof repair close-out. Confirm the draft was created.
